rules.title: Context minimalism
rules.what: Give the model the goal, the constraints and a path to the details (files, search, tools) - not the content itself.
rules.why: Prompt context is processed on every exchange of the turn: tokens processed cost computation, and computation costs energy. Bloat also degrades attention on what matters.
rules.how: State the goal in a short brief; let Vibe read files with read_file/grep instead of pasting them; attach with @path only the few files that matter (an @ mention puts the file in the prompt).

verify.how: Input token count of the prompt is proportionate to the task.

limits: Direction (fewer tokens -> less compute -> less energy) holds; any token-to-watts ratio depends on caching, model, hardware - measure before quoting numbers.

rules.title: Ask the one question that changes the work
rules.what: Ask a blocking question only when a wrong assumption would reshape the work; otherwise state the assumption and proceed.
rules.why: A round trip costs a full model exchange; four questions where one mattered pays three times for nothing. But the one question that changes the architecture is the cheapest exchange of the project.
rules.how: Name the assumption that would reshape the task. Genuinely ambiguous - ask and wait. Otherwise - state it in one line and build.

verify.how: Prompts carry stated assumptions rather than open questions the repository could answer.

rules.title: Let the model fetch on demand
rules.what: The model has read_file, grep and search tools: give pointers, not payloads.
rules.why: Details fetched on demand are processed once, when needed, at exactly the relevant granularity. Details pasted are processed again on every subsequent exchange of the session.
rules.how: File paths and search keywords in the prompt; the model pulls what it needs and keeps the rest out of context.

verify.how: Session input tokens measured against the alternative (pasted content) for the same result.

rules.title: Compact instead of dragging history
rules.what: In a long session, compact deliberately (/compact with instructions on what to keep) and start a new conversation (/clear, alias /new) for unrelated work, rather than carrying the whole history through every exchange.
rules.why: Long histories are re-processed at each exchange; compaction keeps the intents and drops the noise, at a fraction of the tokens.
rules.how: After a milestone: /compact keep the decisions and open issues; for an unrelated task: /clear (optionally seeded with a short brief). Vibe also compacts automatically near 80% of the model window: compacting earlier, with instructions, keeps what matters.

verify.how: Session context size stays within the model's efficient range rather than growing monotonically.

limits: Compaction loses detail; keep decisions in files (docs, decisions.md) the session can re-read.

rules.title: Right model for the task
rules.what: Route the task to the smallest model that meets the quality bar: /model switches; mechanical work does not need the large model.
rules.why: Inference cost scales with model size across every exchange; a large model on a mechanical task pays the difference for identical output.
rules.how: Large model for design, hard debugging and architecture; a smaller one for mechanical refactors, format conversions and doc chores: switch with /model and lower /thinking for routine work. Point [utility_models] (titles, smart-approve classifier) at a small model.

verify.how: Task quality equal on a sample; cost per task lower.

limits: The quality bar is the user's call; the rule forces the deliberate choice, not the smallest by default.

rules.title: Deterministic tools before model reasoning
rules.what: Prefer a deterministic tool (grep, a script, a linter, a validator) over model reasoning for anything a tool decides as well.
rules.why: A grep result is exact, cheap and reproducible; the same question answered by generation pays reasoning tokens for a possibly-wrong answer.
rules.how: Run the script/linter/grep and give the model the output; the model interprets results, it does not emulate tools.

verify.how: Deterministic checks (tests, linters, this skill's audit) back the statements made about the code.

rules.title: One turn, one goal
rules.what: Each prompt pursues one goal; sprawled mega-prompts produce half-done work that needs re-runs.
rules.why: A re-run costs the whole exchange again; work done once at the right granularity is the cheapest. Focus also improves output quality.
rules.how: Split the work into goal-sized prompts; track multi-step work with the todo list (/todo) instead of one sprawling request.

verify.how: Turns end with the goal met or a clear blocker, not with diffuse partial output.

rules.title: No blind retries
rules.what: Retry with new information, not with the same prompt: rewind to before the failed attempt and rephrase, rather than stacking corrections on a wrong path.
rules.why: A retry that varies nothing is the purest waste: same input, same output, same cost. What changes is what you add (a detail, a constraint, a correction).
rules.how: /rewind (or Esc twice) to the message before the wrong turn, then resend with what was missing; /retry only resumes an interrupted response, with optional added instructions.

verify.how: Retried prompts carry an explicit change from the failed attempt.

rules.title: Reuse validated artifacts
rules.what: When a validated artifact exists (a script, a patch, a document), reference it rather than asking the model to regenerate it.
rules.why: Regenerating what exists re-pays generation for a possibly-different result, and reintroduces defects the artifact had already shed.
rules.how: Keep validated outputs as files; the model edits them rather than re-authoring them.

verify.how: Requests target existing artifacts (edit) before creating new ones (generate).

rules.title: Subagents keep the main context clean
rules.what: Delegate exploration and broad scans to subagents; keep the main session for the work that needs the full picture.
rules.why: A subagent's exploratory context (grep results, file dumps) is summarised back, not carried: the main session pays for the conclusion, not the search.
rules.how: Let the model delegate read-only exploration to the built-in explore subagent via the task tool ('explore the codebase and report the call sites'); define narrow custom subagents in .vibe/agents/*.toml with agent_type = "subagent" and minimal enabled_tools.

verify.how: Main-session context growth measured with vs without delegated exploration.

limits: Coordination overhead; delegate bounded, well-scoped explorations.

rules.title: Images only when they carry the task
rules.what: Attach images only when the pixels carry information (screenshots, designs, diagrams); text carries everything else.
rules.why: Vision processing costs multiples of text per unit of information; a task that can be described in three lines does not need a screenshot.
rules.how: Describe in text what text can carry; use images for visual state (UI bugs, design references, error dialogs).

verify.how: Each attached image has a stated purpose the text could not carry.

rules.title: Close what you opened
rules.what: Stop background processes, servers and watchers when done; exit sessions instead of leaving them resident.
rules.why: A forgotten dev server or watcher burns CPU watching a directory nobody is changing.
rules.how: Stop servers and watchers started during the session; cancel recurring prompts you no longer need (/loop list, /loop cancel <id>); exit sessions instead of leaving them resident.

verify.how: No orphaned background processes from the session (process list clean).

rules.title: Group related corrections
rules.what: Gather related corrections and follow-ups into one message instead of serial ping-pong: each message is a full model turn over the whole context.
rules.why: Queued prompts delivered together share one turn's context processing; sequential ones each re-pay the whole exchange.
rules.how: Note follow-ups as they occur; send them together once the current turn ends; review the merged result once.

verify.how: Turns per milestone counted; related corrections sent together.

rules.title: Verify before you regenerate
rules.what: Run the tests/linters before asking the model to 'try again' - the failure may not be in the generated code at all.
rules.why: A regeneration based on an unverified hypothesis re-pays generation for a defect that one test run would have localised.
rules.how: On a failing result: run the check, read the error, give the model the precise failure (paste the decisive line). The actual error message beats 'still broken'.

verify.how: Retry prompts cite the actual error output.

rules.title: Automation proportional to need
rules.what: Hooks and scheduled automation run proportional checks: audit the diff, not the whole repository on every write; schedule heavy scans, not per-keystroke ones.
rules.why: A hook that re-scans everything on every edit multiplies audit cost by edit count; a diff-scoped hook pays only for what changed.
rules.how: Scope hooks.toml entries with match (this skill's post_tool hook only matches write_file|edit and audits the added text), set timeouts, keep post_agent retries rare (Vibe caps them at 3 per turn), schedule heavy scans at a justified interval.

verify.how: Hook runtime per tool call within its timeout budget; scan scope matches the change.

rules.title: Directions, not ratios
rules.what: When discussing the agent's own footprint: state the direction (fewer tokens -> less compute -> less energy), refuse the ratio (tokens to watts/CO2 without measurement).
rules.why: Prompt caching, model size, batching, hardware and grid mix each move the token-to-energy result more than the token count. A quoted ratio without measurement is a fabricated number.
rules.how: Reduce because the computation is real; before quoting any energy figure, measure the actual workload on the actual hardware.

verify.how: No token-to-energy conversion appears without a cited measurement.

rules.title: A complete brief up front
rules.what: Put the goal, the constraints, the acceptance criteria and the pointers to the relevant files in the first message.
rules.why: A vague start costs exploratory turns, each one paid over the full context; a complete brief lets the agent go straight to the work.
rules.how: Goal in one sentence, constraints and done-criteria as a short list, file paths or search terms; leave out what the repository already says.

verify.how: First messages carry goal, constraints and done-criteria.

rules.title: Delegate bounded work
rules.what: Hand the agent a bounded outcome with its verification, then let it work: do not micromanage step by step.
rules.why: Step-by-step steering turns one task into many turns, each re-reading the context; a bounded task with a check lets the agent converge alone.
rules.how: Say what done looks like and how to check it; intervene on results, not on every step.

verify.how: Tasks are stated as outcomes with a check, not as keystroke instructions.

rules.title: No panel of agents for a small task
rules.what: Use several agents or subagents only when the work is broad or parallel by nature; a small task runs in one session.
rules.why: Each agent starts cold and re-reads context; a panel on a small task multiplies compute for the same answer.
rules.how: One session for a bounded change; delegate a subagent for a wide read-only scan; parallelise only independent work.

verify.how: Number of agents used is justified by the size or independence of the work.

rules.title: Bounded, least-privilege headless runs
rules.what: Bound every programmatic run (vibe --prompt) with --max-turns and minimal --enabled-tools, and pass --agent plan for read-only jobs.
rules.why: Headless runs have nobody watching: without a turn cap they can loop, and without --agent Vibe falls back to auto-approve, running every tool call unprompted.
rules.how: vibe --prompt "..." --agent plan --max-turns 5 --enabled-tools read_file --enabled-tools grep --output json; --max-tokens for a hard token cap; treat --max-price as indicative only.

verify.how: CI and scripted invocations set --max-turns, --agent and an explicit tool list.

limits: Vibe's reported cost relies on configured prices that can be missing or outdated; use token counts for hard budgets.

rules.title: Branch before a risky exploration
rules.what: Fork the conversation with /branch before an exploration that may fail, so the main session keeps a clean context.
rules.why: A dead-end exploration leaves its whole trail in the context, paid again at every later turn; a branch keeps it out.
rules.how: /branch, explore in the copy, then resume the main session (vibe --resume <id>) with just the conclusion.

verify.how: Risky explorations happen in a branch; the main session receives the outcome only.

rules.title: Map the code instead of re-reading it
rules.what: Keep a short, maintained code map (key files and their role) and point the agent to it instead of letting it re-read the repository each session.
rules.why: Re-exploring the same codebase every session repays the same file reads; a map lets the agent go to the right file first.
rules.how: A CODEMAP or architecture section in the docs, one line per key module; update it when structure changes.

verify.how: Sessions start from the map; the map matches the current structure.

rules.title: Dense answers, no padding
rules.what: Ask for, and give, answers sized to the need: the result first, no restated question, no generic closing.
rules.why: Every output token is generated, transferred and read; padding costs compute and the reader's attention.
rules.how: Request the format you need (diff, list, one paragraph); keep explanations for what is not obvious from the result.

verify.how: Responses lead with the result and carry no boilerplate.

rules.title: Write the rule once in AGENTS.md
rules.what: Record recurring project conventions in AGENTS.md instead of correcting the agent again each session; keep the file short.
rules.why: A correction repeated each session costs turns every time; AGENTS.md is loaded into every session, so each line in it is paid at every start and must earn its place.
rules.how: Project AGENTS.md for repository conventions, $VIBE_HOME/AGENTS.md for personal ones; one line per rule; remove what the code already shows.

verify.how: Repeated corrections become AGENTS.md lines; the file stays short and current.

rules.title: A skill for what genuinely repeats
rules.what: Package a workflow as a skill only when it repeats; give it a precise description and a narrow allowed-tools list.
rules.why: A skill loads its instructions only when relevant, instead of re-explaining the workflow each time; a vague or overbroad skill loads too often and grants too much.
rules.how: SKILL.md in .vibe/skills/<name>/ (reviewable in code review) or ~/.vibe/skills/; description that names when to use it; allowed-tools minimal; user-invocable for explicit runs.

verify.how: Each skill covers a repeated workflow, with a precise description and minimal tools.

rules.title: Commit messages and PRs for the next reader
rules.what: Write commit messages and pull-request descriptions that state what changed and why, so the next reader (human or agent) does not have to rediscover it.
rules.why: History that explains intent saves later investigation sessions and repeated code reading.
rules.how: Subject line with the intent; body with the reason and trade-offs; link the issue; no generated filler.

verify.how: Commits and PRs state the why, not only the what.

rules.title: Give the agent a way to check its work
rules.what: Provide a proportionate verification loop (tests, a linter, this skill's audit, a command that shows the result) so the agent checks its work instead of guessing.
rules.why: Without a check, errors surface later and cost new sessions; a cheap deterministic check closes the loop in the same turn.
rules.how: Name the command that proves done (make test, the validator, a curl); keep it fast; scale it to the change.

verify.how: Each task names the check that proves it done, and the check ran.

rules.title: Least privilege for the agent
rules.what: Run the agent with the least privilege the task needs: plan for exploration, default or accept-edits for normal work, auto-approve only in a sandbox; trust only folders you have reviewed.
rules.why: Broad permissions let a mistaken or manipulated tool call do real damage, and rework after damage costs far more than an approval prompt. Reliability and ethics are part of Numérique Responsable.
rules.how: Shift+Tab or --agent to pick the agent; per-tool permissions in config.toml; review .vibe/, AGENTS.md and hooks before trusting a folder; smart-approve is a classifier, not a sandbox.

verify.how: Agent and permissions match the task; auto-approve only in isolated environments.

rules.title: Inclusive, accessible generated content
rules.what: Ask for, and check, generated docs, UI text and messages that are inclusive and accessible: gender-neutral and people-first wording, plain language, alt text, sentence-case headings.
rules.why: The agent writes at scale: biased or inaccessible wording is replicated in every file it touches, excluding readers and users (IT for Social).
rules.how: Put the expectation in AGENTS.md; review generated text with the Mistral inclusive-language guide; use 'they', 'people with disabilities', and describe images.

verify.how: Generated text reviewed against the inclusive-language guide; images carry alt text.
